newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron University students defy closure order.
newsitem.headline: Hebron University students defy closure order.

text.p: Palestinian students broke into the campus of Hebron University to resume classes on Monday, defying an Israeli military closure that has shut the school since March, witnesses said.

About 10 Israeli military jeeps ringed the campus after some 300 students and faculty members entered the university vowing to study even at the risk of clashes with Israeli troops, the witnesses said.
"It is our right to study at our own university," said Ahmed Abu Snaineh, a student.
"Yigal Amir killed the prime minister of Israel and they did not close his university," he said, referring to the law student who shot dead Yitzhak Rabin last year.
Witnesses said students brought crates of onions to neutralise the effects of tear gas in case Israeli troops decided to storm the campus.

Members of the Palestinian Legislative Council were trying to mediate an agreement that would allow the students to study. Witnesses said soldiers took up positions on buildings around the campus and that Israeli authorities were insisting the students leave the compound.
"We support the students in their peaceful protest to open their university," Jamal al-Shoubaki, a legislator told reporters.
Israel closed Hebron University in March during a wave of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel in which 59 people were killed. The closure order has kept more than 1,500 students out of class.
The university organised student registration in October at a location near the campus but students were not able to study.

Hebron is the last West Bank city that Israel agreed to hand over to the PLO under a self-rule deal signed last year. But the Hebron redeployment has been delayed by Israeli demands for better security arrangements for about 400 Jewish settlers who live or study in Hebron amidst more than 100,000 Palestinians.
Israel handed six major Palestinian towns to the PLO last year.

Intensive talks between Israel and the PLO with U.S. and Egyptian mediation have failed so far to bring the two sides closer to an agreement on implementing the Hebron redeployment deal signed by Israel's previous government.
